title: Renal Cell Carcinoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2027 clinical navigator for Kidney Cancer / Renal Cell Carcinoma. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (high-resolution multiphasic renal CT/MRI, chest CT, germline screening for VHL/MET/FH/BAP1/FLCN, mass biopsy indications) -> Localized Surgical Management (partial vs radical nephrectomy, ablation, active surveillance for cT1a) -> Adjuvant Immunotherapy (KEYNOTE-564 Pembrolizumab Category 1 with overall survival benefit for intermediate-high, high, or M1 NED) -> Advanced / Metastatic Clear Cell RCC stratified by IMDC Risk (Favorable vs Intermediate/Poor) -> Frontline IO-TKI and IO-IO regimens -> Second-line and Subsequent Therapies (LITESPARK-005 Belzutifan Category 1 post-IO/TKI, Cabozantinib, Nivolumab, Tivozanib) -> VHL-associated RCC (Belzutifan Category 1) -> Non-Clear Cell RCC (Papillary, Chromophobe, Medullary, Collecting Duct with Cabozantinib and Lenvatinib + Pembrolizumab). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Kidney Cancer Version 1.2027.

a.text: IMDC (International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium) risk model: 0 factors = favorable, 1-2 = intermediate, 3-6 = poor. Factors: less than 1 year from diagnosis to systemic therapy, Karnofsky PS under 80, anemia (hemoglobin below lower limit of normal), hypercalcemia (corrected calcium above upper limit), neutrophilia, thrombocytosis.

b.text: Adjuvant pembrolizumab for 1 year (KEYNOTE-564, Category 1 Preferred) improved disease-free survival with a statistically significant overall survival benefit (HR 0.62) in resected clear-cell RCC at intermediate-high risk, high risk, or M1 NED. Weigh against immune-related toxicity.

c.text: Dual checkpoint blockade (nivolumab + ipilimumab, CheckMate 214, Category 1 Preferred) is preferred for intermediate/poor-risk clear-cell disease; benefit is less established for favorable-risk disease, where an IO-TKI combination is preferred.

d.text: Non-clear-cell RCC is biologically heterogeneous; enrollment in a clinical trial is preferred where available. Cabozantinib is Category 1 preferred for metastatic papillary RCC (SWOG S1500); lenvatinib + pembrolizumab is Category 2A preferred for non-clear-cell disease (KEYNOTE-B61).

e.text: Reassess disease with cross-sectional imaging (RECIST-style) at defined intervals; separate pseudoprogression on immunotherapy from true progression before switching lines. Response or durable stable disease continues therapy; unequivocal progression or intolerable toxicity triggers the next line.

f.text: Belzutifan (HIF-2alpha inhibitor, LITESPARK-005, Category 1 Preferred) is preferred for advanced clear-cell RCC progressed after both a PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor and a VEGF inhibitor. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia.

g.text: Belzutifan (Category 1 Preferred) is indicated for VHL disease-associated RCC not requiring immediate surgery. Monitor for anemia and hypoxia.

nodes.name: Diagnostic workup
nodes.title: Diagnostic workup for suspected or confirmed RCC
nodes.description: Complete baseline evaluation of a renal mass before choosing a management pathway.
nodes.path: Renal Cell Carcinoma / Workup
bullets: History and physical examination, Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) / ECOG PS.
Laboratory baseline: Complete blood count (CBC), comprehensive metabolic panel (CMP with BUN, creatinine, eGFR, alkaline phosphatase, AST/ALT, bilirubin), corrected serum calcium, urinalysis.

Cross-sectional diagnostic imaging: High-resolution multiphasic contrast-enhanced CT or MRI abdomen and pelvis with dedicated renal mass protocol (pre-contrast, corticomedullary, nephrographic, and excretory phases) to assess tumor size, renal vein / IVC thrombus, and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
Distant staging: Chest CT (without contrast or with contrast) for mandatory pulmonary metastasis screening; brain MRI if neurologic symptoms; bone scan if elevated alkaline phosphatase or bone pain.

Renal mass biopsy: Recommended when mass is small (<3 cm) and active surveillance/ablation is considered, before initiating systemic therapy for metastatic disease, or when histology would alter surgical strategy (e.g. suspecting lymphoma, abscess, or metastasis).

Hereditary RCC screening: Recommend genetic counseling and germline testing for patients age <=46 years, bilateral or multifocal tumors, or personal/family history of RCC or associated syndromes (VHL, HLRCC/FH, Birt-Hogg-Dube/FLCN, hereditary papillary/MET, BAP1-tumor predisposition).
